settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of optimizing a fixed and unknown function $f: \cX \to \R$, where $\cX \subset \R^d$ is a compact domain and $f \in \cH_k$ with $\|f\|_{\cH_k} \leq B$. A sequential optimization algorithm chooses a point $x_t \in \cX$ at each time $t$ and observes $y_t = f(x_t) + \varepsilon_t$. In the noise-free setting, $\varepsilon_t \equiv 0$ for all~$t$.

source.label: thm:noiseless_regret
source.quote: Assume that the kernel $k$ satisfies the polynomial eigendecay condition with parameter $\beta > 1$ and function $f$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assumption:f_level_set_regularity}. For a given $\delta \in (0,1)$, if REDS algorithm is run with $N_1 \geq C_{L_f, L_f'} \overline{N}(\delta/\log_2(T))$ and noise-free feedback, then the regret incurred by REDS satisfies, R(T) = \tilde{\cO}(\max\{T^{\frac{3-\beta}{2}}, 1\}). with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

results.notes: Regret is realized regret of deterministic f, holding w.p. 1-delta. Claimed to match lower bound of Tuo & Wang (2020), resolving COLT open problem.

source.label: thm:noisy_regret
source.quote: Consider the noisy observation model described in Sec.~\ref{sub:problem_formulation} and assume that Assumptions~\ref{ass:discretization} and~\ref{assumption:f_level_set_regularity} hold. For a given $\delta \in (0,1)$, if REDS algorithm is run with $N_1 \geq C_{L_f, L_f'} \overline{N}(\delta/(2\log_2 T))$ and UCB and LCB functions ... with parameter $\delta' = \delta/(2 \log_2 T)$, then the regret incurred by REDS satisfies, R(T) = \tilde{\cO}(\sqrt{T\gamma_T} \log(T/\delta)). with probability at least $1 - \delta$.

results.notes: gamma_T is maximal information gain with noise parameter tau. Regret is realized cumulative regret w.p. 1-delta.
